correctness.rationale: On a labelled simple cycle of length at least three, the two neighbors are distinct and the centered triple checks are exactly the two feasibility conditions. Summing b−1+h(a,b)−h(b,c) telescopes to w−n; all 20 allowed triples have nonnegative reduced cost and precisely the 16 displayed edges have cost zero. Thus the all-one word attains the minimum and the critical closed walks count all minimizers without quotienting rotations. Independently, merging identical successor rows first gives classes {00,10}, {01}, {02}, {11,21}, {12,22}, {20}; the resulting rows for {01} and {02} then coincide. On the five quotient classes A={00,10}, G={01,02}, D={11,21}, E={12,22}, F={20}, the equations for I−xZ reduce by unit-pivot elimination to A=xG, F=x(A+G), E=xF, D=G+xA and (1−x−2x³−x⁴)G=0. The eliminated directions contribute only zero eigenvalues. The trace identity gives the logarithmic series; the length-one and length-two traces are both 1 and must be removed. A fresh brute force check using the feasibility predicate alone gave weight n and multiplicities 7, 13, 16, 31, 64 at lengths 3–7. The quartic has a primitive nonnegative companion matrix (a loop and a spanning directed 4-cycle), so the unique leading eigenvalue is positive and simple, and its trace contribution has coefficient 1. Replay: reconstruct the zero-edge rows from RESULT.md lines 35–71, then use the quotient equations or the integer determinant recipe. The finite check is corroboration only; the result does not count nonoptimal words or dihedral orbits.
